scope: Segment DL1 host-originated, separator-free, self-delimited (Data Type '#' ... End-of-Data '~') merchant and accepted-card-type download segment carried in Data Block No. 1 of the Table Load Response
extractionEvidence: regression-artifact-validator/specifications/ATL105/docs/specs/extracted_text.txt lines 17101-17206 (Section 12.42), 8968-9236 (Section 11.7.1 Table Load), 19587-19604 and 20591-20608 and 21693-21700 (Section 13.2 Elements 4, 53, 54, 98), 26245-26330 (Appendix E Table Load card types)

rules.title: Segment DL1 maximum length is 399 alphanumeric characters; originates at BUYPASS (Host)
rules.note: 399 = 1 (#) + 24 + 16 + 24 + 21 + 13 + 2 + 99 x 3 (Card Type) + 1 (~): the maximum is reached only with 99 Card Types and every fixed field at full width.

rules.title: Segment DL1 uses NO Field Separators; instead it is self-delimited by a Data Type Indicator ('#', field 1) and an End-of-Data Indicator ('~', last field) — a distinct delimiting convention from the numbered segments (85/84 Segment Type/Length pair)
rules.note: Segments DL1-DL6 use this Data-Type/End-of-Data marker convention instead of the Segment Type(85)/Segment Length(84) pair used by numbered segments 100-157. DL1 has no Segment Length field.

rules.title: Merchant Name(53,24), Store Number(98,16), Address Line 1(3,24), Address Line 2(4,21), Merchant Phone Number(54,13) are all required, Host-sourced fixed-length fields
rules.note: Elements 53, 3 and 98 are defined as 'fixed length of up to N'; the padding convention is open under P-02.

rules.title: Number of Card Types (Element 59) identifies how many times field 8 (Card Type) repeats — Card Type may repeat 01-99 times
A Card Type value of '173' in this segment's repeating Card Type field (Element 14) conditionally triggers Segment DL6 (Store and Forward) in the same Table Load Response
Segment DL1 fields are not separated by Field Separators; when a field is not populated, the next field immediately follows (no empty-position placeholder is kept)
rules.note: Segment 100's 'keep the separator for an empty middle field' rule does NOT apply. Because every DL1 field is Required, an unpopulated field is itself a defect; the parse boundary for 'up to N' fields depends on P-02.

rules.title: Segment DL1 is Required in the Table Load Response, carried as Data Block No. 1 immediately after the Start-of-Data Block Indicator (Element 97, fixed ')'), and is sent only on a Table Load Response
rules.note: The Chapter 12 'Data Segments and the Transactions in which They Can Appear' matrix (page 12-5) marks DL1 for the Table Load Response only.

rules.title: A Table Load takes place only when the merchant profile load flag is TABL; when the flag is not set, the Downline Load Response contains only an error message block and a terminating block, so Segment DL1 must be absent
rules.note: The paired Table Load Request (11.7.1.1) carries Information Byte '?', Terminal Identifier, Load Type 'P', Hardware, Software and Firmware Version and no DL segment.

rules.title: Each repeated Card Type (Element 14) must be a valid Appendix E 'Card Type Code Used in the Table Load Response': an accepted card type or a device feature code (for example 127, 148, 150, 162-168, 171, 173, 174); feature codes are never used in Prompt Codes
rules.note: The Appendix E introduction quotes ranges 001-086 and 127-168, but the table also lists 088-096, 150, 171, 173 and 174; the complete valid set is open under P-04.

rules.title: Address Line 2 (Element 4, 21 characters) is positional: positions 1-12 city, 13 space, 14-15 alphabetic State Code (Appendix D), 16 space, 17-21 ZIP Code

Merchant Phone Number (Element 54) is 13 characters in the form (nnn)nnn-nnnn; Store Number (Element 98) is numeric in the range 0000000000000001-9999999999999999 and, when masked with asterisks, is neither displayed nor printed

Table Load Response block order is ')' + DL1, then DL2 (Conditional), then DL3 (Conditional), then End-of-Load Indicator '*' (Element 35); when DL1 carries Card Type 173, DL6 (Data Block No. 4) follows and the load ends with '*'. For TCP/IP the Start-of-Data Block Indicator appears only before Data Block No. 1
rules.note: The device parses each block by its Data Type Indicator. Whether '*' is sent both after DL3 and after DL6 is open under P-03.
